title: Integration Boost is computed per block from venue USDS balances against the Sky Savings Rate
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.5.2.2.1.1.7 — the Kamino Instance's Savings Rate Adjustment Strategy — states that "the Integration Boost is calculated based on per block values for USDS in Kamino and the Sky Savings Rate."

Two choices are compressed into that sentence. First, the boost is defined *relative to the Sky Savings Rate* rather than as an independent reward: the subsidy exists to close the gap between what a partner venue can pay on USDS and what holding sUSDS would have paid, which is what makes depositing into the venue rationally comparable to staying in Sky's own savings product.

Second, both inputs are sampled per block. That prevents the two classic gaming patterns of period-averaged incentive programs — parking capital only at snapshot time, and arbitraging a rate that moved mid-period — because a deposit earns boost only for the blocks it was actually present, at the rate that actually prevailed.

The cost is measurement burden: a per-block calculation over a Solana venue and an Ethereum-set rate cannot be eyeballed, which is precisely why the same parameter set delegates computation to a named actor and publishes the result through an API endpoint. Precision in the formula creates dependence on the pipeline that evaluates it.
description: Keel's boost tops up partner-venue yield relative to the Sky Savings Rate at block granularity, so the subsidy tracks the actual rate gap rather than a flat advertised APY.
